cases.event: One night during a full moon, observers at {E} watched the moon grow dim and turn a dull reddish color.
cases.q: What most likely caused the full moon to grow dim as seen from {E}?
restate: The full moon grew dim as seen from {E}, and the question asks why.
Something caused the full moon to look dim and reddish from {E}.
cases.answer: Earth's shadow falling across the moon most likely caused the dimming, because the shadow blocked sunlight from reaching the moon's surface.
cases.sum: the evidence points to Earth's shadow as the cause of the dim, reddish moon.
cases.myth: The moon grew dim because it ran low on its own stored light.
cases.mythClause: the moon dims whenever it gets tired
cases.cause: Earth's shadow falling across the moon
cases.altText: Some visitors suggested that thin clouds drifting over {E} had dimmed the moon.
cases.patternQ: What pattern connects the dark curved edge and the brightness of the moon seen from {E}?
cases.patternA: The moon dimmed as a curved shadow moved across it and grew bright again once the shadow moved off, so the brightness followed the shadow.
cases.patternSum: the moon's brightness fell and rose as the shadow moved across it and away.

prediction.text: Earlier that evening, a visitor predicted that the dimming would be seen only from {E}.
prediction.claim: the dimming would be seen only from {E}
prediction.whyNot: observers in a faraway town saw the same dimming at the same time

cases.observerNote: The observers took a photograph of the moon every five minutes.

obs.text: An astronomy chart showed that Earth's shadow would cross the moon that night, and the dimming began right on schedule.
exps: the dimming began exactly when the shadow was expected, which points to the shadow as the cause
a prediction that matches the event this closely ties the dimming to Earth's shadow
the timing lines up with the shadow, not with the weather

obs.text: A curved, dark edge slowly moved across the face of the moon during the dimming.
exps: a curved edge is the shape a round planet's shadow would make, which shows the shadow at work
this shows how the moon lost its light, since a shadow was blocking the sunlight
the moving edge is the shadow itself sliding across the moon

obs.text: After about {n0} minutes, the dark edge moved off the moon and it shone brightly again.
exps: the moon brightened as soon as the shadow moved away, which is what would happen if the shadow were the cause
the dimming ended when the shadow ended, so the two are linked
once the cause moved on, the effect disappeared

obs.text: Weather records showed that the sky over {E} was completely clear all night.
exps: clouds cannot have dimmed the moon on a night with no clouds
this rules out clouds, because the sky was clear
with no clouds overhead, the cloud explanation has nothing to stand on

obs.text: Observers in a town {n1} kilometers away saw the same dimming at the same time.
exps: clouds are local, so they could not dim the moon in the same way for two distant places
this rules out clouds, since a faraway town saw the identical change
a change seen from far apart places fits a shadow on the moon itself, not something in the local sky
predExps: this directly contradicts the prediction, since a faraway town saw the dimming too
if the dimming could be seen only from {E}, the distant observers would have seen nothing unusual, but they did
the prediction expected a local event, and the observations show a widespread one
